questions.question: Which one among the following statements regarding the properties of mixtures and compounds is NOT correct?

options.text: A mixture shows the properties of its constituents but the properties of a compound are entirely different from its constituents
Energy is either absorbed or evolved during the preparation of a mixture but not in the preparation of a compound
The constituents of a mixture can be separated by physical methods but those of a compound cannot be separated by physical methods
A mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous but a compound is homogeneous

questions.solution:
Option **2** is **NOT correct.**

 
• The **compound** is **always formed by absorption or evolution of energy** but **no energy is released or absorbed during the formation of the mixture. Hence, Option 2 is NOT correct.**
 
• The mixture contains two or more substances mixed, but neither chemically as well as not in inexact quantity while compound includes two or more elements combined chemically and in a fixed ratio.
 
• A mixture shows the properties of its constituents but the properties of a compound are entirely different from its constituents
 
• Mixtures do not have a certain formula.
 
• A mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
 
• The constituents of a mixture can be separated by physical methods
 
• Compounds have a specific formula, depending on the constituents present.
 
• A compound is homogeneous.
 
• Constituents in a compound cannot be separated by physical methods.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true for pure substances?

(i) Pure substances contain only one kind of particles

(ii) Pure substances may be, compounds or mixtures

(iii) Pure substances have the same composition throughout

(iv) Pure substances can be exemplified by all elements other than nickel
questions.solution:
**Concept**

**Homogenous mixture: **

__
 
• This mixture has a uniform composition and appearance.
 
• Individual substances of a homogeneous mixture cannot be visually differentiated.
 
• Examples: Air, Sugar water, Rainwater, etc.

**Heterogeneous mixture:**

 
• This mixture comprises two or more substances that can be distinctly observed and even separated relatively easily.
 
• Examples: Sand, oil and water, chicken noodle soup, etc.

**Explanation__:**

**Pure substance:**

 
• A pure substance consists of a **single type of particle**. 
 
• A substance is a pure single form of matter.
 
• Pure substances have the **same composition throughout**.
 
• A pure substance may be **either a compound or an element**.
 
• Examples, **Hydrogen gas, Gold metal, Sugar, Baking soda** (sodium bicarbonate), Ammonia, etc.

**Mixture:**

 
• These are constituted by **more than one kind of pure form of matter**.
 
• Most of the matter around us exists as mixtures of two or more pure components.
 
• For example, **seawater, minerals, soil,** etc. are all mixtures.

**Examples: **

 
• **Crude oil:** A mixture of organic compounds (mainly hydrocarbons)
 
• **Seawater**: A mixture of various salt and water.
 
• **Air:** a mixture of various gases like oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, argon, neon, etc.
 
• **Ink:** A mixture of coloured dyes.
 
• **Gunpowder:** A mixture of sulfur, potassium nitrate, and carbon

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct for a heterogeneous mixture?

options.text: The composition of the mixture is uniform.
A clear solution is called a heterogeneous mixture.
Mixtures don't contain physically distinct parts.
The composition of the mixture is non-uniform.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A heterogeneous mixture has a **non-uniform composition**, meaning its components are not evenly distributed throughout the mixture.
 
• In a heterogeneous mixture, the different parts of the mixture are **physically distinct** and can often be seen as separate phases.
 
• Examples of heterogeneous mixtures include **sand in water** and **oil in water**, where the components do not blend into a single phase.
 
• Heterogeneous mixtures are characterized by **visible boundaries** between the different components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixture**

 
 
• A homogeneous mixture has a **uniform composition** throughout and its components are not distinguishable.
 
• Examples include salt dissolved in water and air.
 
• In homogeneous mixtures, the different components are present in a single phase.
 
 
 
• **Physical Distinction in Mixtures**
 
 
• In heterogeneous mixtures, the different substances can often be separated by physical means such as filtration or decantation.
 
• Physical distinction means that the individual components maintain their properties within the mixture.
 
 
 
• **Solution**
 
 
• A solution is a type of homogeneous mixture where one substance (the solute) is dissolved in another (the solvent).
 
• Solutions are typically clear and do not exhibit the Tyndall effect.
 
 
 
• **Colloids and Suspensions**
 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where the particle size is intermediate between those in solutions and suspensions, and they exhibit the Tyndall effect.
 
• Suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures where the particles are large enough to settle out over time.

questions.question: During filtration process, the particles which remain on filter paper is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**residue.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Filtrate -

 
 
• **The filtration process **is used to separate an** insoluble solid from a liquid.**
 
• After this process, the solid which collects in the filter paper is called the **residue.**
 
 

 
• **Solute -**

 
 
• The solute is a substance that dissolves in a solvent, that is, it has a **dissolving nature.**
 
 
 
• **Solvent -**
 
 
• **That medium **in which the solute is dissolved is **called the solvent.**
 
• For example, if **lemon is dissolved in water** to make lemonade, the lemon will be soluble and the **water will be solvent.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The element that is formed by mixing the solute and solvent is **called a solution.**
 
• Both solute and solvent have properties inside the **solution.**
 
• **Different Types of Solutions-**
 
 
• Depending upon the dissolution of the solute in the solvent, solutions can be categorized into supersaturated solution, unsaturated and saturated solutions.
 
• A supersaturated solution comprises a large amount of solute at a temperature wherein it will be reduced, as a result, the extra solute will crystallize quickly.
 
• An unsaturated solution is a solution in which a solvent is capable of dissolving any more solute at a given temperature.
 
• A saturated solution can be defined as a solution in which a solvent is not capable of dissolving any more solute at a given temperature.

questions.question: Which among the following is **not** the property of a solution?

options.text: A solution can be separated by filtration.
It can only be done when solute is solid.
Solute particles will settle down when left undisturbed for a while.

questions.solution:
**__Concept:__**

**Solution: **

__
 
• A solution is a **homogenous mixture **of two or more components with particles less than one nanometer in size.
 
• Sugar in water and salt in water solutions, as well as soda water, are common examples of solutions.
 
• All of the components of a solution appear as a single phase.
 
• There is **particle homogeneity** or a uniform distribution of particles.
 
• A solution is made up of two parts:** a solvent **and **a solute**.
 
• The solvent is the part of the solution that dissolves the other components (typically the ones that are present in greater amounts).
 
• The solute is the part of the solution that dissolves in the solvent (and is usually present in smaller amounts).

**Properties of a solution:**

 
• It's a completely **uniform** mixture.
 
• Its particles are too **small**, with a diameter of less than 1 nanometer.
 
• The particles can't be seen with the naked eye.
 
• A beam of light moving through particles does not scatter, therefore the path of the light is not apparent.
 
• Solutes are inextricably linked to the rest of the mixture and** do not settle.** 
 
• **Filtration cannot separate **the constituents of a solution.
 
• A solute can be a solid, liquid, or gas.
 
• A solvent too can be of any state - solid, liquid, or gas. 

**Explanation:**__

 
• The given three statements provide are not the correct properties of a solution, 
 
• A solution can be separated by filtration - a false statement as a solution can not be separated with the help of filtration. The particles are uniform throughout hence filtration is not the correct technique for separation 
 
• It can only be done when a solute is solid - a false statement as solute as well as the solvent can be of any state - solid, liquid, or gas. 
 
• Solute particles will settle down when left undisturbed for a while - a false statement as solute particles are completely soluble hence they don't settle down. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is - **All of the above are not **properties of a solution**. **

questions.question: A solution contains 50 g of sugar in 450 g of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of mass by mass percentage of the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10%**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To **calculate the mass by mass percentage of the solution**,

 
 
• we **need to divide the mass of sugar by the total mass of the solution (sugar + water) and then multiply by 100%.**
 
• **Total mass of the solution:** 50 g (sugar) + 450 g (water) = 500 g
 
• **Mass by mass percentage:** (50 g sugar / 500 g solution) * 100% = 10%
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass percentage** is a way to express the concentration of a component (like a solute) in a mixture (like a solution).
 
• It tells you how many grams of that component are present in 100 grams of the total mixture.
 
• **Calculation of Mass percentage**
 
 
• **​**Mass percentage = (Mass of component / Total mass of mixture) * 100%

questions.question: A solution contains 40 ml of acid in 120 ml of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of volume by volume percentage of the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Volume by volume percentage is calculated using the formula: frac{{Volume of solute}}{{Total volume of solution}} times 100.
 
• Here, the volume of the solute (acid) is 40 ml.
 
• The total volume of the solution is the sum of the volume of the solute and the solvent: 40 {ml} + 120 {ml} = 160 {ml}.
 
• Using the formula: frac{40 {ml}}{160 {ml}} times 100 = 25\%.
 
• The concentration in terms of volume by volume percentage of the solution is 0.25 or 25%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concentration units**

 
 
• Concentration can be expressed in various units such as molarity, molality, mass by volume percentage, and volume by volume percentage.
 
 
 
• **Applications of concentration**
 
 
• Concentration is a critical factor in chemical reactions, pharmaceuticals, and solutions in various industries.
 
 
 
• **Importance of accurate measurements**
 
 
• Accurate measurements of solute and solvent volumes are essential for precise concentration calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about suspension?

options.text: A Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Solids dispersed in gas are called suspensions.
Particles of a suspension are invisible to the naked eye.
A Suspension is a homogeneous mixture.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Suspensions** are mixtures where particles are dispersed throughout the bulk of a fluid.
 
• The **particles in a suspension** are larger and can be seen with the naked eye or under a microscope.
 
• **Suspensions are heterogeneous**, meaning the components are not uniformly distributed.
 
• The particles in a suspension will **settle over time** if left undisturbed.
 
• **Examples** of suspensions include sand in water, flour in water, and chalk in water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solutions**

 
 
• These are homogeneous mixtures where the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent.
 
• Examples include salt dissolved in water and sugar dissolved in tea.
 
 
 
• **Colloids**
 
 
• These are mixtures where very small particles of one substance are evenly distributed throughout another substance.
 
• Examples include milk, mayonnaise, and fog.
 
 
 
• **Emulsions**
 
 
• A type of colloid where two immiscible liquids are mixed together, with one liquid dispersed in the other.
 
• Examples include vinaigrette and certain cosmetic creams.

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is correct regarding the properties of suspension?

I. Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

II. The particles of a suspension can be seen by the naked eye.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mixtures are of two types: Homogenous and Heterogeneous.
 
 
• **Solutions are homogeneous mixtures.**
 
 
 
• **Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture of solid particles in a fluid**.
 
 
• ​If the particles in a solution are not settled down, then it is a suspension.
 
 
 
• Particles in a suspension are bigger compared to a solution and** look cloudy due to non-uniformity.**
 
• **Because of the colour, the suspensions can be seen with the naked eye. Hence option 3 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are two phases in suspensions, they are internal and external.
 
 
• The external phase is the dispersion medium or continuous phase and is fluid.
 
• The internal phase or dispersed phase is made of particulate matter which is insoluble in the external phase.
 
 
 
• **In solutions, the particles are dissolved in the liquid completely** and do not settle down.
 
 
• So, **you cannot see the solutions** or they are completely transparent.​

• Colloids are big enough to scatter a beam of light passing through it and make its path visible.

• The size of solute particles is large enough to be seen by the naked eye.

• This is like an unstable solution. The solute particles settle when left undisturbed.

The solute particles cannot be seen by naked eyes in colloids but can be seen in the suspension. 

So, the statement 'T__**he solute particles can be seen by naked eyes in colloidal solution as well as in suspension' **__is incorrect and **hence the correct option. **

questions.question: Which of the following will show the “Tyndall effect” ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch Solution**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tyndall effect is the mechanism in which the particles in a colloid scatter the rays of light that are directed at them. **

 
 
• **All colloidal solutions and some very fine suspensions exhibit this effect. **
 
• Therefore, it can be used to **confirm if a given solution is a colloid. **
 
• **Scattered light intensity depends on the colloidal particle density as well as the incident light frequency.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Examples of the Tyndall effect**__

 __
 
• Milk makes of a colloid comprising fat and protein globules. The light is spread when a beam of light is directed at a glass of milk. This is a perfect description of the Tyndall effect.
 
• The direction of the light becomes evident when a torch is turned on in a foggy atmosphere. The water droplets in the fog are accountable for the scattering of light in this case.
 
• Opalescent glass has a bluish appearance when viewed from the side. However, orange-colored light emerges when light is shined through the glass​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tyndall Effect Responsible for Blue Eye Colour**

 
 
• **The primary difference between blue, brown, and black colored irises is the amount of melanin in one of its layers**. The layer in a blue iris has relatively lower amounts of melanin in it when compared to a black iris, making it translucent. When light is incident on this translucent layer, it is scattered due to the Tyndall effect.

questions.question: The diameters of colloidal particles may range from :
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**Understanding the Size Range of Colloidal Particles**

__
 
• Colloids are mixtures where one substance (dispersed phase) is evenly dispersed in another substance (dispersion medium) without settling over time.
 
• For a mixture to be classified as a colloid, the particle size of the dispersed phase must fall within a specific range, which is typically between 1 nm and 1000 nm.
 
• This size range is crucial because it allows colloidal particles to exhibit unique properties such as:
 
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** Colloidal particles scatter light, making the light path visible. This phenomenon is observed when a beam of light passes through colloidal dispersions.
 
• **Stability in Suspension:** Colloidal particles do not settle under the influence of gravity due to their small size and interactions with the dispersion medium, allowing the colloid to remain stable over time.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** Colloidal particles exhibit random, zigzag motion due to collisions with molecules of the dispersion medium. This motion prevents them from settling and contributes to their stability.
 
 
 
• Particles smaller than 1 nm generally dissolve completely in the dispersion medium to form a true solution, where individual molecules or ions are present.
 
• Particles larger than 1000 nm tend to form suspensions. In a suspension, particles are large enough to settle over time due to gravity, and they do not exhibit colloidal properties.

**EXPLANATION**__:

__
 
• To identify the correct size range for colloidal particles, consider the general classification of particle sizes in different types of mixtures:
 
 
• **True Solutions:** Particles are typically smaller than 1 nm. Examples include salt in water or sugar in water, where individual ions or molecules are completely dissolved.
 
• **Colloidal Solutions:** Particles range from 1 nm to 1000 nm. Examples include milk, fog, and gelatin. These particles are small enough to remain dispersed without settling but large enough to scatter light.
 
• **Suspensions:** Particles are larger than 1000 nm. Examples include sand in water or muddy water. These particles are large enough to settle out over time, making suspensions unstable compared to colloids.
 
 
 
• Since colloidal particles fall in the range of 1 nm to 1000 nm, they display the intermediate properties between true solutions and suspensions.

**CONCLUSION:**__

**The correct option is:** **Option 1) 1 to 1000 nm**

**Consider the following statements. **

I. The particles settle down when remain left undisturbed. 

II. The particles can be seen easily with naked eyes. 

III. The mixture may show the Tyndall effect. 

In which of the following mixture the above all characteristics can be observed?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Properties of a colloid-

__
 
• A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture.
 
• The size of solute particles of a colloid is too small (10 -7 m) to be individually seen by naked eyes.
 
 
• So, solute particles cannot be seen by naked eyes.
 
 
 
• Colloids are big enough to scatter a beam of light passing through it and make its path visible.
 
 
• This is also known as Tyndall Effect. 
 
 
 
• They do not settle down when left undisturbed, that is, a colloid is quite stable
 
• They cannot be separated from the mixture by the process of filtration. But, a special technique of separation known as centrifugation, can be used to separate the colloidal particles.

Properties of a suspension

 
• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture
 
• The size of solute particles is large enough to be seen by the naked eye.
 
• They can also show the Tyndall effect when rays of light pass through them. 
 
• This is like an unstable solution. The solute particles settle when left undisturbed. 

**Properties of Solution**

 
• A solution has solute particles in the range of 10 ⁻ ⁹ m in diameter. 
 
• The salt solution in water or sugar solution in water are examples of the solutions. 
 
• Solute particles can not be seen by naked eyes. 
 
• The particles cannot be separated by filtration or decantation. 

**Explanation:**__

The given properties in the question are 

I. The particles settle down when remain left undisturbed. 

II. The particles can be seen easily with naked eyes. 

III. The mixture may show the Tyndall effect. 

All these implies to suspension. 

__**Mud water is an example of a suspension and hence the correct option**__

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a heterogeneous mixture?

options.text: The composition varies throughout the mixture.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The composition varies throughout the mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** is one where the components are not evenly distributed, and the **composition varies** throughout the mixture.
 
• It often consists of physically distinct parts, each with **different properties**.
 
• Examples of heterogeneous mixtures include **salad, sand and water, or oil and water.**
 
• In such mixtures, the individual components can typically be **separated using physical methods**, such as filtration or sorting.
 
• The heterogeneous nature of the mixture means that its appearance is often **non-uniform**, and you can see the different substances visually.
 
• This type of mixture contrasts with a **homogeneous mixture**, which has a uniform composition throughout.
 
• Heterogeneous mixtures play a significant role in various fields, such as **geology, chemistry, and material science**, for studying and separating substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: It has a uniform composition**__

 __
 
• This describes a **homogeneous mixture**, not a heterogeneous mixture. Homogeneous mixtures have the same composition throughout, such as **salt dissolved in water**.
 
• These mixtures appear visually uniform and are often referred to as **solutions.**
 
 
 
• **Option 2: The components cannot be separated**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect for heterogeneous mixtures because their components can often be **physically separated**. For example, sand and water can be separated through **filtration.**
 
• This description is more suitable for **compounds**, where components are chemically bonded and cannot be separated by physical means.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It contains only one phase**__
 
 
• This characteristic applies to **homogeneous mixtures**, where only one phase (solid, liquid, or gas) is present.
 
• Heterogeneous mixtures often consist of **multiple phases**, such as oil and water, which exist as separate liquid phases.

questions.question: Which of the following sets comprises physical changes?

options.text: Shredding of paper, baking a cake, bursting of crackers
Boiling of water, cooking of food, rusting of iron
Burning of paper, setting of milk into curd, breaking a glass
Breaking of glass, grinding wheat, boiling of water

questions.solution:
**__Concept__ :**

**Physical changes :**

__
 
• Properties such as shape, size, color, and state of a substance are called its **physical properties.**
 
• A change in which a substance undergoes a change in its physical properties is called a **physical change.**

**Explanation __:**

__
 
• A physical change is generally **reversible**.
 
• In such changes, **no new substance** is formed.
 
• Examples of physical changes are **breaking glass, boiling water, and grinding wheat.**
 
• In the above examples only the physical properties of glass, water, and wheat change.

**So, the correct answer is Breaking glass, grinding wheat, boiling water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Chemical changes :**

 
• A change in which **one or more new substances **are formed is called a chemical change.
 
• A chemical change is also called a** chemical reaction. **
 
• All new substances are formed as a result of chemical changes.
 
• Examples of chemical changes are **digestion of food in our body, ripening of fruits, fermentation of grapes, **etc., which happen due to a series of chemical changes.
 
• Medicine is the end product of a chain of chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f968f5674e0e631a04d2ec9805b05c156915e2852763a4f03cc18b87f7e828d.png] ​
